title: DeepSeek V4 Pro on iac-bench 2026-11
summary: How DeepSeek V4 Pro did on iac-bench 2026-10: an overall composite of 69.2, scores per fixture, strengths, weaknesses and the patterns in its OpenTofu modules.

## Summary


DeepSeek V4 Pro is close to the leading group on S3 (G001, median 82) and falls well behind on Cloud SQL and App Service. All 9 of its modules planned. Five of the 9 had a security finding, each caused by a security setting exposed as an input or left at an insecure provider default.


Its most distinctive weakness is documentation that describes behavior the code does not implement. The judge scored *Documentation* 0 in all six of its Cloud SQL and App Service attempts.

Definitions are in[Scoring criteria](https://www.massdriver.cloud/blogs/iac-bench-2026-10-scoring-criteria) .


## Strengths


- **Every module planned** (9/9).
- **S3 baseline coverage.** Bucket-owner-enforced ownership, multipart cleanup and the regional domain output in 3/3 attempts, and a TLS-only policy in 2/3. The judge gave one S3 attempt *Scope* 2 "without unwarranted extras."
- **Dedicated resources.** *Inline vs separate resources* scored 2 in 8/9 attempts.
- **No password users on Cloud SQL.** Only IAM users are created.
- **One App Service attempt meets every core and mandatory item** (rubric 0.944). The model knows the settings, but applies them inconsistently.


## Weaknesses


- **Security findings (5/9):**


- S3, one attempt: all four public-access-block settings are fed by` var.block_public_access` (` H1` ).
- Cloud SQL, two attempts:` ipv4_enabled` is an input. In one it defaults to` true` , so the defaults plan has a public IP, while the description says "Private-only regardless of this flag" (` H1` ). In the other,` require_ssl = false` maps to unencrypted connections (` H1` ,` H2` ).
- App Service, two attempts: the basic-auth publishing flags are never set (` H2` ). One attempt also makes` https_only` an input (` H1` ).


- **Documentation that contradicts the code.** Examples:


- "least-requests load balancing" that is never configured;
- a` staging_traffic` input documented to route traffic, which only feeds an output;
- "0 disables autoresize", which it does not.


- **Lifecycle misuse.**` prevent_destroy = var.deletion_protection` in 3/3 Cloud SQL attempts, duplicating the native` deletion_protection` attribute. *Lifecycle meta-arguments* scored 0 in all three.
- **Inputs declared and never used,** in several attempts (` zone` ,` allocated_ip_range` ,` staging_traffic` ,` service_tag` ).


## Characteristic patterns


- **The stated posture and the actual interface disagree** (excerpt below).
- **It leans toward too many inputs.** One S3 attempt has 18 inputs, one Cloud SQL attempt 34. *Interface design* scored 1 in 9/9.
- **Stray files on Azure,** such as` _tmp_prod.tf` and` _full_test.tfvars` , and a pinned` azurerm ~> 3.0` with deprecated arguments in one attempt.


## Representative excerpt


` G002/deepseek-v4-pro-0813-e3/main.tf` lines 30–38


```text
ip_configuration {
ipv4_enabled    = var.ipv4_enabled
private_network = var.network


allocated_ip_range = var.private_ip_allocated_range


# TLS posture on the (opt-in) public path. Private path traffic never
# leaves the VPC, but SSL is still enforced end-to-end for defense in depth.
ssl_mode = var.require_ssl ? "TRUSTED_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED" : "ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_AND_ENCRYPTED"


```


The comment says SSL is enforced end to end, and the next line lets a caller turn it off. Public IP is also an input.
